Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in decoupling crosslinking's chemical (covalent bonding) effects from its physical (structural) effects in starch/chitosan-derived hard carbon, isolating each contribution to sodium-ion anode performance. This mechanistic separation enables rational molecular engineering of biomass precursors, offering a design principle to optimize hard carbon anodes for high-performance sodium-ion batteries rather than relying on empirical crosslinking.

Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a capacity–electrochromism decoupling strategy: a bilayer cathode spatially separates optical readout from high-capacity storage, enabling real-time state-of-charge monitoring in high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. Significance: it achieves 3.4 mAh cm⁻² with 97.8% retention over 300 cycles and a monotonic SOC–Hue relationship at 1% intervals, offering built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.

item.title: Carbonyl‐Rich Polyimide Covalent Organic Frameworks as Anode Coating for Uniform Sodium Deposition
item.description:
این مقاله دو COF پلی‌ایمیدی غنی از کربونیل را به‌عنوان پوشش آند باتری سدیم فلزی معرفی می‌کند که رسوب یکنواخت Na و پایداری چرخه‌ای بالا را بهبود می‌دهد.
Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in designing two isocyanurate-based polyimide COFs with abundant carbonyl ion-binding sites and ordered frameworks as artificial anode coatings. This enables uniform sodium deposition, dendrite suppression, and stable cycling (1200 h symmetric; >90% retention after 1390 cycles at 5 C). It demonstrates rational carbonyl-rich 2D COF design as a significant strategy for durable sodium metal battery anodes.
🏷 sodium metal battery · covalent organic framework · anode coating · uniform Na deposition · polyimide COF
